scale_note: Millimeters are explicit designed requirements in the original source and literal brief. No scale is inferred from preview pixels.
assumptions: Original proposed inspection instrument, not a recovered manufacturer BOM, calibrated comparator or approved factory design.
All local dimensions, poses and primitive recipes beyond the explicit source callouts are chosen design assumptions. The complete v2 basis map documents these choices without asserting source truth.
Screws are connected one-piece head/shank envelopes. Threads and recipient holes are omitted, so overlap at a fastened interface is an unresolved manufacturing feature, not joint validation.
Saddles, bushings, collar, bezel, housing and stem have modeled bores. Running and clamping clearances are proposed, not toleranced fits.
Dial gearing, spring, spindle, glass, graduations, seals, retainers, drive recesses and lubrication are omitted. The face marks in the original drawing are graphics rather than physical parts.
Parts that touch or overlap do not establish fastener engagement, detachable joints, collision-free travel, stiffness or calibration. One stationary inspection pose is proposed.
Manufacturing notes per definition are proposals only. Actual material, process, finish, datum scheme, tolerances, loads and factory acceptance require responsible human review.

observations.statement: The original source identifies an invented bench-comparator design proposal with millimeter dimensions and no manufacturer BOM claim.
The front view shows a bed, feet, left column and L arm, round front-facing dial, vertical contact and separate coupon on a rail carriage.
The top view shows twin guides, four saddles, end stops, a rectangular carriage, rear-left post and right-side travel datum.
The source states bed 240 x 150 x 12 mm, four feet, rods diameter 8 x 170, dial diameter 50, dial center Z125 and coupon top Z51.
The source states rod centers Y +/-27 and Z27, carriage 60 x 76 x 6 and post diameter 12.
The source calls the subassemblies proposed, omits internal gearing and threads or recipient holes, and leaves fits, tolerances, materials, calibration and factory processes unconfirmed.

frame.why: Chosen right-handed Z-up millimeter frame. Bed bottom is Z0; +Y points rearward. Zero Euler rotations and zero local offsets are authoring conventions.

metric.why: The original designed brief and drawing explicitly use millimeters. This scale is a proposed design requirement, not a measured physical product.
